gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Chunky bent-straw lettering, curled shut at the ends. Plakkaat stays closed and uniform in stroke while Noto Sans Lepcha opens its curves wide, and that tension is the pair's best trait.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Stencil-cut weight, heavy and bent like straw. Plakkaat keeps its letters closed at a constant thickness, while Noto Sans Limbu gapes open with tall-bodied lowercase, and that opposition is the whole appeal.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-mandaic: Bold Plakkaat sets a heavy, stencil-cut tone with one steady width. Noto Sans Mandaic then reads smoothly across many lines, its lowercase rising near capital height and its curves loose and unclamped.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-mayan-n: Plakkaat sweeps its terminals around until they nearly touch the stem, giving heavy bent-straw letters a closed look. Noto Sans Mayan Numerals brings the opposite: a gaping c, tall-bodied forms.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-myanmar: Heavy monoline lettering curled like bent straw, with Plakkaat taking the lead. And Noto Sans Myanmar carries a broad-mouthed c and a dense middle band that reads smoothly line after line.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-nabatae: Plakkaat curls its terminals back toward the stem, so every heavy letter looks nearly closed. Noto Sans Nabataean runs loose and open underneath, its near cap-tall lowercase and generous s curves reading easily over many lines.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-nag-mun: Noto Sans Nag Mundari brings half-unwrapped curves and near-capital lowercase. Plakkaat, traced at a single stylus width, supplies the dense closed heading while the sans-serif text beneath loosens everything up.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-newa: Noto Sans Newa looks generous on the page, with a clearly open lowercase e and tall counters and bowls. Plakkaat, closed and heavy above it, supplies the sharpest opposition.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-old-ita: Plakkaat squeezes every stroke out in one steady line. Noto Sans Old Italic, a sans-serif with almost no gap between lowercase and capitals, keeps its curve endings apart for the opposite feel.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-old-per: Noto Sans Old Permic reads friendly and rounded, its curves open to the side and its lowercase nearly capital height. But Plakkaat, with no calligraphic thinning anywhere, supplies the solid weight that makes this pair work.
